newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH BOURSE SEEN REGAINING GROUND NEXT WEEK.
newsitem.headline: POLISH BOURSE SEEN REGAINING GROUND NEXT WEEK.

text.p: The Polish bourse is likely to regain ground next week as this week's profit-taking correction after an 11.6-percent gain since mid-August seems to be slowing down and could end on Monday or Tuesday, analysts said.
They said technical analysis showed that though slight falls could follow the expected rebound, the market was unlikely to fall below 13,000 points of the main WIG index.
"The bourse should rebound on Monday or on Tuesday, and the correction should end above 13,000 or even above 13,500 points," said Wojciech Kossuth of Bank Slaski brokerage.
But some analysts said the bourse could extend losses to 12,300 points of the WIG before rebounding, which they saw happening in about two weeks. The WIG fell 2.6 percent this week to 13,568.1 points

Analysts said the ruling left-wing coalition crisis, which followed the sacking of foreign trade minister Jacek Buchacz on Wednesday, could slow down the expected growth next week, but was unlikely to cause a plunge unless the coalition collapsed.

They said the bourse's performance next week might also be influenced by investors speculating before the release of companies' August earnings reports, but that this was likely to affect mainly small-cap companies vulnerable to speculation.

"There will probably be speculation, mainly on smaller stocks, so (reports) shouldn't have a decisive impact on the whole WIG, but there certainly will be some sharp movements," said Pawel Hominski, an analyst at Magnus brokerage.

Analysts said they expected the results, most of them due from September 16 to September 18, to match July earnings in being slightly better than those shown in the first half of this year and to help keep the market mood good.
Mass privatisation NFI units beat their July debut of 104 zlotys rising 9.9 percent on the week in record turnovers, and analysts expected them to keep rising.
Analysts said this week's top gains and falls were accidental and could not be explained by fundamental basis.
The week's biggest losers on the main market were Rolimpex , KPBP Bick , and Boryszew , down 12.3 percent, 11 percent and 9.3 percent respectively.
The top gainers were Farm Food , Bytom and Espebepe , up 12.2 percent, 9.8 percent and 7.7 percent respectively.
